expectations.text: Wrote translate/SPEC.md containing at least ten numeric measurements in logical pixels before the first Codex build

expectations.evidence: Loads bytedesk.tokens.css (vendored) but contains two colour literals: --studio-inset: #14171A and .btn-primary color: #fff. Also pulls Google Fonts, which the token sheet already governs.

expectations.evidence: No translate/prompts/*-r1.txt, no attempts.json, no codex log; RESULT.md describes the executor measuring, mapping tokens and writing the page itself. Claude authored the markup inline.

expectations.evidence: screenshot-1280x800.png exists (1280x800), but there is no diff/report.json, no layoutScore, no hotspots. RESULT.md says 'compared against the mockup' with no artefact.

expectations.evidence: No patch prompts, no diff observations, no FROZEN list. RESULT.md mentions 'one iteration to tighten sidebar type' with no recorded justification. 1 round (plus one undocumented tweak).

expectations.text: Reported layoutScore as the mockup comparison and never presented pixelDiff against the mockup PNG as the pass/fail number
expectations.evidence: No layoutScore or pixelDiff reported at all; no comparison number of any kind. Cannot pass an assertion about which metric was presented.

expectations.text: state.json lists every screenshot and diff image read under stages.translate.viewed
The final round's report.json shows layoutScore ≥ 0.95 against the mockup (structural fidelity, not just process)
expectations.evidence: No report.json for any round, so no layoutScore. Visual read of the screenshot vs the mockup shows real structural drift: runs list starts ~40px higher, timeline wraps the first line ('...prompt and\ncontext.'), Retry button smaller, attempts table positioned differently, right-column brief wraps to 5 lines with different breaks, composer moved. Structurally similar but not measured.

expectations.text: No hex or rgb() colour literal anywhere in the surface HTML (HTML entities such as ▸ are not colours)
expectations.evidence: Same two literals as above: '#14171A' and '#fff' (entities like ▸ excluded from the scan).

critique: Baseline 0/10. The executor produced a plausible, reasonably faithful page (token-driven, correct content, right three-column shape) but none of the contract artefacts exist: no spec, no Codex hand-off, no diff/report, no state.json, no numeric comparison. The two hex literals and the built-in link underlines are exactly the failure modes the skill's spec-first / invented-element rules target. Fair note for the eval author: assertions 3/10 are the only ones the baseline could have passed by good taste alone, and it still didn't; the rest are process artefacts the skill defines, so a baseline near zero is expected and the discriminating signal is genuinely assertions 3, 9 and 10.
